title: RecomputeReport
description: The impact-analysis + rebuild record of a derived recompute (roadmap Phase 5.3), the FINAL link that closes the prose→fact evolution loop: after a mint advances a fact (mint-receipt.schema.json), every derived artifact pinned to that fact — directly or TRANSITIVELY (a fact advances → the ChapterDraft pinned to it goes stale → everything derived from that draft goes stale) — is stale and must not be consumed as truth (ADR-006). Staleness DETECTION already existed (runtime/derived.py); this report records the recompute's response to it. The response is a DETERMINISTIC/GENERATIVE PARTITION, mirroring the discipline of the whole system: a derived artifact that is a PURE FOLD of facts (e.g. StoryState — reproducible, no model, no cost, no outward act) is AUTO-REBUILT here, written back with a fresh pin so it is no longer stale; a GENERATIVE artifact (prose ChapterDraft, quality review, reader/commercial simulation — produced by a model, an outward creative act) is NEVER auto-rebuilt (re-authoring reviewed prose would silently clobber it), it is STAGED as 'regeneration required' with the exact human command to regenerate it. This makes the recompute engine to derived artifacts what the mint executor is to facts: it executes only the safe deterministic work and stages the rest behind the human-authority boundary (ADR-009). Two structural invariants: `authority` const human — a generative rebuild is a human-authorized regeneration, the report stages it, never triggers it; and `gating` const false — a recompute report is an audit record, it does not gate a build (ADR-003). Written to registry/derived/recompute-reports/, NEVER to registry/facts/ (a recompute report is not a story fact, and this subdomain is not a fact-writer — only runtime/mint/ is, ADR-006).

authority.description: Structural invariant (ADR-009): regenerating a generative artifact is a human-authorized act. This report auto-rebuilds only pure deterministic folds; it STAGES generative work for a human, never triggers it.

gating.description: Structural invariant (ADR-003): a recompute report is an audit record, not a build gate.

trigger.description: What made the impacted set stale. Normally a mint (the 5.2→5.3 chain); may also be a direct scan of the provenance index against the current registry.

kind.description: mint = driven by a MintReceipt's advanced entities; scan = audited the whole index vs the current registry.

advanced_entities.description: The fact ids (with their new version) whose advance triggered this recompute — carried for audit.

impacted.description: Every stale derived artifact this recompute considered, with why it is stale and what was done. The complete impact set (rebuilt ∪ staged ∪ any that could not be classified).

category.description: The derived category dir (drafts, story-state, quality, ...).

kind.description: deterministic = a pure fold of facts, safe to auto-rebuild; generative = produced by a model, must be regenerated by a human.

staleness.description: direct = pinned to an advanced fact; transitive = pinned to another artifact (e.g. a draft) that went stale.

action.description: rebuilt = deterministically recomputed + written back this run; staged = left stale, a human regeneration command recorded.

rebuilt.description: The deterministic folds auto-rebuilt this run — each written back with a fresh pin so it is no longer stale.

content_hash.description: The rebuilt artifact's content_hash (byte-reproducible from the current facts).

content_hash_changed.description: Whether the rebuild changed the artifact's content_hash (a fact advance need not change every projection).

path.description: Where it was written under registry/derived/.

staged.description: Generative artifacts left stale for a human to regenerate — with the exact command. NOTHING was written for these; the loop deliberately stops at the human-authority boundary (ADR-009).

regenerate_with.description: The human command that would regenerate this artifact (e.g. 'runtime execute --task … / runtime refine …'). Descriptive; the report never runs it.
